device.name: Open Duck Mini v2 (BDX_env humanoid MuJoCo environment)

facts.text: BDX_env is registered with entry point env_humanoid:BDXEnv, max_episode_steps=None (formerly 500) and autoreset=True
The observation space is a Box of 41 float64 values with no finite lower or upper bound
The healthy base height range is 0.1 to 0.2 metres
The episode terminates when the base is unhealthy or its local z-axis is not upright
The reward weights are forward_reward_weight 1.25, ctrl_cost_weight 0.3 and healthy_reward 5.0
The environment runs 5 MuJoCo physics steps per environment step (frame_skip 5)
The reward is healthy_reward minus ctrl_cost (0.3 times the sum of squared controls) minus moving_cost (twice the absolute x velocity)
The observation concatenates the joint positions, the joint velocities and the left then right foot contact flags
A reset adds uniform noise between -0.01 and 0.01 to the initial positions and velocities
The BDX model defines 15 position actuators: five per leg plus neck_pitch, head_pitch, head_yaw and the two antennas
The base body starts at height z=0.17 metres
The scene's timestep option is commented out (the comment says 100 Hz), so the clone states no active physics timestep
The environment declares render_fps 100 in its metadata
Open Duck Mini is about 42 centimetres tall with its legs extended

determinism.notes: reset(seed) or cap.world.seed.v1 fixes the fake's initial noise and the fake dynamics are deterministic, so one implementation repeats a trajectory for the same seed and actions; the fake draws with Python's random.Random and upstream draws with numpy's generator, so one seed gives different trajectories on the two

gaps: kinematic stand-in, not MuJoCo: an action sets the 13 joint positions directly and the joint velocities are their per-tick differences; there are no rigid-body dynamics, contacts, friction, actuator, sensor or noise model, the two foot contact flags are constants and termination never fires in the fake

the action table of env_humanoid.py:24-36 has 13 rows with a duplicated index 9, while mini_bdx/robots/bdx/robot.xml:284-298 defines 15 position actuators; the declared 41-value observation corresponds to 13 joints (20 qpos + 19 qvel + 2 contacts), whereas the 15-joint model would give 45 values; the fake follows the declared 41-value space, so the neck_pitch and antenna channels are NOT COVERED and the upstream environment's declared space and its model disagree

the upstream environment was not run: it imports placo (env_humanoid.py:4) and builds its scene from the absolute path /home/antoine/MISC/mini_BDX/mini_bdx/robots/bdx/scene.xml (env_humanoid.py:105), outside the clone
the reset noise comes from Python's random.Random, upstream from numpy's generator; states and observations are Python floats, upstream returns a float64 NumPy array

the real action space is built by gymnasium's external MujocoEnv and is not stated in the clone; the fake's Box boundaries are placeholder test data (not a sourced device bound) and the derived action.values limits are only the bridge's view of that stand-in
no rendering and no snapshot/restore: the environment exposes no get_state/set_state in the clone, so snapshot_restore is false and the render_modes metadata is not served by cap.world.*

timestep_ms is 0 because the clone states no active physics timestep (scene.xml:2-3 comments the 100 Hz option out) and the fake is event-driven: one tick is one environment step, not a fixed duration
no physical device is modelled and the fake was never validated against the upstream environment

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: an e-stop latches and every step or reset is refused until mhs.safety.reset clears it, while the fake environment keeps its state and stays readable
